transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

No — a displayed time of about 3 hours 39 minutes on Eco 40–60 is normal, and by itself is not a sign that the machine is faulty.

“Eco 40–60” is the programme used for the energy-label testing. It saves electricity and water mainly by:

• heating the water more slowly and often to a lower actual temperature than a conventional 40 °C wash;
• washing for longer, with soaking and gentler drum movement;
• adjusting parts of the cycle according to the load, water temperature and detergent/foam level.

So it can be the longest programme on the machine, despite being the most economical in energy use. A conventional older “40 °C” cycle lasting around an hour was likely using more water and/or more heating energy.

A few useful distinctions:

• Eco 40–60: best for normally soiled cottons and lowest energy use; expect roughly 3–4 hours.
• Cottons 40 °C / Synthetics 40 °C: usually more conventional wash times, though often still longer than an old machine.
• Quick/rapid programme: suitable for small loads that are lightly soiled; not normally ideal for towels, bedding, or heavily soiled clothes.
• If your machine offers Time Save, it may shorten some programmes, usually at the cost of extra energy/water or reduced washing performance. It may not be available with every cycle and option.

The time shown at the start is also an estimate; it may move a little as the machine senses the load.

I would not send it back just because Eco 40–60 takes 3:39. Consider contacting AEG/the retailer only if it repeatedly runs far beyond the displayed time, shows an error, fails to heat, leaves clothes consistently dirty, leaks, makes abnormal banging/grinding noises, or does not complete cycles.
